items.headline: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
items.blurb: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
items.text: Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort. Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin. items.headline: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19
items.blurb: Russia's Defence Ministry says preliminary findings for the crash point to equipment failure.
items.text: A military plane has crashed in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, according to a statement from the Russian Defence Ministry, cited by local media. The Antonov An-12 transport aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000km east of Moscow. The An-12 typically has a crew of six. Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash, but preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure. “A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by the RIA Novosti news agency. Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk, posting on Telegram from the scene of the accident, said emergency crews had extinguished a fire. He said crews were helping to investigate the accident. Seredyuk, in a video posted online showing the site of the accident near the village of Yagunovo, said the plane had been flying through the region when it crashed. items.text: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”. The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country. In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”. items.headline: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
items.blurb: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.
items.text: Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula. A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before". But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures. The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday. For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. items.headline: US Fed’s Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
items.blurb: US President Donald Trump has been trying to fire Cook since August 2025.
items.text: United States Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has declined, through her lawyers, to appear next month before a Trump administration committee that is considering whether she should be fired, calling the process unfair and committed to a predetermined outcome. The refusal extends the wrangling between the White House and Cook’s lawyers regarding her appearance before the committee, which the administration of US President Donald Trump initially demanded for November 6. Administration officials have called on Cook to appear before the committee to address allegations that she committed mortgage fraud in 2021, before she joined the Fed’s board of governors, a charge she denies. Cook has not been charged with any crime. Trump has sought to fire Cook since August 2025, and she has argued that the president’s efforts to do so represent a threat to the Fed’s independence and reflect Trump’s desire to force the central bank to reduce borrowing costs. “Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding

items.headline: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities
items.blurb: Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.
items.text: An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country. Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates. The NDLEA said the player told them he had come to Nigeria to “build networks” for his basketball career. The agency said evidence on his phone suggested he had “knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity”. The NDLEA said it detained the player when he attempted to leave the airport with his hand luggage after abandoning two checked-in bags. The agency said those two bags were found to contain 32 parcels of marijuana, and a tracking device. Nigeria has strict drug laws, and trafficking carries a sentence of life in prison. A basketball player by the name of Damonte Greene is listed on the roster of the Pattani Raptors in the Thai Premier Men’s League.

items.headline: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
items.blurb: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
items.text: Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia if the board asked him to, in his first public comments since his shock resignation. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. He said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia. But, as the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company. The company's board is investigating his conduct , which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive. The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang. items.blurb: UK authorities have passed the investigation to the US 'in line with existing international protocols'.
items.text: A senior United States soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to US military custody, United Kingdom police have said. The Head of Counter Terrorism Police (CTP), Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, said on Tuesday that authorities in London have passed the investigation to US partners “in line with existing international protocols”. The 41-year-old man was arrested by British police on November 10 near Gloucester on suspicion of offences under Section 1 and Section 3 of the UK National Security Act 2023. Section 1 relates to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while Section 3 relates to assisting a foreign intelligence service. “These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place,” Taylor said. items.blurb: Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to…
items.text: Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city. The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved. The growth in both baboon and human populations in Cape Town in recent years has led to increased conflict and more baboons dying as a result. Meanwhile, a heated debate has raged between people who believe that baboons and humans can coexist and those who argue that baboons in urban areas are in danger and in some cases need to be relocated. items.headline: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
items.blurb: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
items.text: The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions. Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted. Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around. At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide. The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours. Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet. items.blurb: An Eastern Assam-based environment activist writes to the Supreme Court-constituted Central Empowered Committee, highlighting the concerns
items.text: A building at an advanced stage of construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve in November 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve. Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months. In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order. “We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including

items.headline: Quad leaders unveil initiatives to boost Indo-Pacific trade, connectivity; oppose coercion
items.blurb: PM Modi joined US President Donald Trump, Australian PM Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for the Quad Leaders Summit in Manila.
items.text: The leaders of the four Quad nations met in Manila on Tuesday for the first time in more than two years, reiterating their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific and unveiling new initiatives meant to bolster maritime surveillance, trade and connectivity across the region. Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined US President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for the Quad Leaders Summit, which – without naming China – opposed unilateral actions to alter the status quo by force or coercion and expressed concern over economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions. This was Trump’s first Quad Summit and came ahead of his participation in a meeting of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum to be hosted by China's President Xi Jinping, who has objected to the Quad as an effort to encircle Beijing, and a trilateral meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US on Thursday. “For India, the Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership. items.headline: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
items.blurb: Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter
items.text: A view of the Badrinath Temple, nestled between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges on the bank of the Alaknanda river. File. | Photo Credit: PTI Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year. According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard. Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025. The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added. To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. items.text: Union minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi on Tuesday called those criticising ethanol blending in petrol as “idiots who do not know the science behind it”. The Union MoS' remarks came while addressing a youth dialogue in his parliamentary constituency of Thrissur. "Those spreading allegations (about E20 petrol) have twisted political thinking. They are idiots who do not know the science behind it. From first to last, they are idiots," the minister said. He also alleged that those making such claims and testing ethanol content in fuel may be buying petrol in canisters and mixing something in it before taking samples. "And then, we may have to call in the CBI to probe such claims. These people will then turn against the CBI also," he further remarked. Gopi argued that ethanol blending from E10 to E20 in petrol was introduced after “scientific research and re-research” by the Automobile Research Association of India. items.blurb: He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts
items.text: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah addresses the foundation stone-laying ceremony on November 17, 2026. Photo: X/@CM_JnK. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that companies from the outside must hire locals and that hiring outsiders will not be allowed. “The excuse that trained youths are not available will not work. We will provide you (companies) six months or one year and prepare our youths. We also have ITIs (Industrial Training Institutes), polytechnics, colleges, and universities,” said Mr. Abdullah. The J&K Chief Minister said youths from J&K have no shortage of talent. “They (youths) only need opportunities. We will not tolerate excuses at the cost of our children’s future,” said Mr. Abdullah. He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts. items.headline: Italian tourist found dead in Manali hotel
items.blurb: An Italian tourist was found dead in his hotel room at Chanala-Jagatsukh near Manali in Himachal Pradesh, police said on Tuesday.
items.text: An Italian tourist was found dead under suspicious circumstances in his hotel room at Chanala-Jagatsukh near Manali in Himachal Pradesh, police said on Tuesday. According to the police, Faraday Michael did not step out of his room for about a day. Suspecting something had gone wrong, the hotel management informed the Manali police station on Tuesday. When police opened the room, they found Michael lying dead on the bed with no injury marks on his body, officials said. His passport, cash, a mobile phone and some medicines were found in the room. Michael was a heavy smoker, and it is believed that he was suffering from asthma, police said. Police have informed the Italian Embassy in Delhi about the incident after sending the body to a mortuary in Manali. Further action will be taken as per rules, they said.

items.blurb: Emerging-market currencies rebounded as the dollar halted a five-day rally, while developing stocks retreated for a fourth straight session with Nvidia Corp.’s earnings in focus.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Emerging-market currencies rebounded as the dollar halted a five-day rally, while developing stocks retreated for a fourth straight session with Nvidia Corp.’s earnings in focus. The MSCI gauge of emerging-market currencies rose on the day, snapping a three-day losing streak, as the dollar extended losses and oil advanced amid fresh flareups in the Middle East. The greenback is breaking a five-day winning streak, dropping as much as 0.2% after CNN reported that the highly classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its internal communications is down. But developing-world currencies may still struggle for direction. Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem signaled support for multiple interest rate-increases in the coming months. His New York counterpart John Williams said the central bank still has work to do to bring inflation back to its goal, but dismissed the suggestion the Fed needs to consider an outsized rate increase. items.headline: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it not reinstating Huang
items.blurb: Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang earlier on Tuesday offered to return, despite the board's disinterest.
items.text: Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it is not reinstating ousted founder Jensen Huang. In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Collette Kress said Nvidia's "roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater". The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company recovering some recent losses in after-hours trading. Earlier on Tuesday Huang, said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a possible spy for China. "The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones told investors on Tuesday. The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same time period. Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise another 13%

items.blurb: DEUTSCHE BANK-MEDIA/SEWING (ANALYSIS, PIX):ANALYSIS-Deutsche Bank leaks test CEO Sewing's pledge to reform
items.text: FRANKFURT, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Leaked internal documents detailing Deutsche Bank's dealings with Russian oligarchs and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein dealt a major setback on Tuesday to CEO Christian Sewing's efforts to restore the lender's reputation. The documents included emails, meeting minutes and internal records that media organisations said showed Deutsche Bank pursued Russian business right up until Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine and handled more suspicious transactions linked to Epstein than previously known. The reports also said the bank mistakenly shared Donald Trump's tax records with another client's accountant. Deutsche Bank dismissed the revelations as historical, saying it had spent €7 billion ($7.7 billion) strengthening compliance and controls since 2019. Chairman Alexander Wynaendts publicly backed Sewing, who took over in 2018 with a mandate to restore profitability and rebuild trust in Germany's largest lender. Sewing has largely delivered on the first goal, returning Deutsche Bank to sustained profitability after years of losses. The company’s board has allotted 12,870 equity shares and 22,523 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 31,079 per share to raise the capital, according to documents reviewed by Entrackr . Ayra Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 45 crore, while Waterfield Advisors invested Rs 15 crore and A91 Partners infused Rs 10 crore. Ithought Financial Consulting LLP invested Rs 10 crore through an equity allotment in August 2026, while the co-founders collectively invested Rs 7.2 crore. The remaining amount came from several other investors. The proceeds will be utilised to fund the company's growth and expansion plans, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes. As per Entrackr’s estimates, the latest allotment values Shree Anandhaas at around Rs 1,908 crore, a 3.3X jump from its Series A valuation of Rs 575 crore.

items.text: Actor Ranveer Singh and boAt co-founder Aman Gupta have joined hands to launch H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man), a men's personal care brand targeting the growing grooming market in India. The brand has launched eight products across skincare, haircare and body care, with prices ranging from Rs 299 to Rs 899. With this move, the company will compete with established players such as The Man Company, Ustraa, Beardo, HUL’s Minimalist, BSC, and others. The initial range includes face wash, moisturiser, sunscreen, body wash, body lotion, soap, shampoo and scalp serum. The products are available through the brand's website, Amazon and Blinkit. According to the company, H.I.M has been developed specifically for Indian men's skin and local weather conditions, including heat, humidity, pollution and hard water. The products are powered by IN-XT, a proprietary delivery system. The firm said it conducted 408 laboratory trials over 16 months of research and testing. More than 150 Indian men across different skin types and complexions were also part of the testing process. Unlike several celebrity-led personal care brands, Singh is joining Gupta as a co-founder.

Speaking at a news conference conference in Dublin on Monday before the Springboks' match with Ireland, Erasmus questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?". The two-time Rugby World Cup-winning coach was referencing the implementation of new rules surrounding hip-drop and knee-drop tackles, and felt the laws were not being applied correctly. It comes after Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast became the first player to be cited for a hip-drop tackle in Ireland's win over Fiji on Saturday , which was not penalised in-play by referee Angus Gardner and television match official TMO Mike Adamson. items.text: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. items.headline: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
items.blurb: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t.
items.text: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors. For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses. AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built. We will not make AI trustworthy by predicting what it will do. items.headline: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
items.blurb: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate.
items.text: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together, turning AI from a collection of tools into part of the enterprise operating model. For Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, that shift begins with treating AI as an enterprise platform rather than a collection of disconnected projects. “AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation,” he says, arguing that companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes. The stakes also change as AI moves into mission-critical workflows. items.blurb: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially…
items.text: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”

items.blurb: The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
items.text: Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors. Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022. Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis. Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April. items.headline: Perplexity May Launch IPO As Early As Q1 CY27: CEO Aravind Srinivas

items.text: Perplexity may file for an IPO as early as Q1 CY27, with CEO Aravind Srinivas saying its ARR has crossed $1 Bn. The accelerated IPO timeline has put Perplexity on course to potentially join OpenAI and Anthropic in the public markets. Perplexity's growth has been supported by its India push, which became the startup’s biggest market following strategic partnership with enterprise players. AI major Perplexity has preponed its proposed IPO timeline and could file its draft IPO papers for a listing in the US as early as Q1 2027. Speaking with CNBC, founder and CEO Aravind Srinivas revealed that Perplexity has managed to grow faster than expected which pushed the decision to fast-track the listing. “The rate at which our business is growing, I wouldn’t rule out filing something in the first quarter of 2027,” Srinivas said during the broadcast. As per him, the company has already touched an ARR (annual recurring revenue) of $1 Bn, surpassing its $750 Mn ARR expectations ahead of the IPO. items.headline: Claude Outpaces ChatGPT, Gemini In India Adoption

items.text: Claude became the third-ranked app in terms of consumer spending on in-app purchases while ChatGPT maintained its leading position The data signals consumers’ shifting preferences for AI apps as global players compete for a slice of the Indian market that is projected to grow to $126 Bn by 2030 While ChatGPT’s revenue from in-app purchases increased by 70% YoY, Claude’s grew 15X, in line with its download growth Anthropic’s AI bot Claude is close on the heels of Indian AI market leader ChatGPT, with the former’s adoption outpacing OpenAI’s offerings significantly over the past few months. Downloads for Claude in India jumped 15X in the September quarter compared to the same period last year, as per data released by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. Meanwhile, downloads of ChatGPT declined by 21% over the same timeframe. However, the app maintained its position as India’s market leader among GenAI apps. items.headline: AI adoption, weak demand to keep India's IT services revenue growth subdued in FY27: Report
items.blurb: India's IT services sector may continue to face subdued revenue growth in the remaining months of FY27 as rising adoption of artificial intelligence shifts technology spending towards AI-focused companies and reduces demand for traditional services, according to a report by ICICI Securities.
